title: The Four Thieves
hook: A consent script behind a closed clinic door can stop a thief before it enters.
counterintuition: The trap is noticing thieves after they have already taken the hour. Defense has to be visible before time, structure, or attention is stolen.

keyTakeaway: Defend focus by naming the thief in advance and placing a practical barrier before it arrives.

It is asking which demand deserves first contact because steal focus will change the next layer of reality. That is why the first move must be chosen by effect, not by comfort.. Something should open, shrink, clarify, or become unnecessary. If nothing changes, choose again with a sharper eye.

implementationPlan.coreSkill: You learn to use The Four Thieves as a decision skill, not a slogan. The skill is to identify the recurring threats that steal protected focus and build defenses before they enter the room. and then act before easier work takes the lead.

ifThenPlans.plan: If competing requests open the workday, then choose the request that changes the next decision and handle it before status tasks.
If a study session starts broad, then identify the concept that unlocks the largest number of problems and begin there.
If household tasks crowd the day, then choose the action that lowers the most friction for the people involved and do it first.
If a meeting has several valid topics, then make the consequence-changing topic the first agenda item and move updates after it.
